name: 8BitScript
_comment: Tracks the syntax the project has specified so far: the TypeScript-derived
surface, the machine integer types, the hardware escape hatches
(@address decorators, volatile/ptr/array, and asm6502 blocks), and the
compile-time functions (#frames(...), #system()), the reserved runtime builtin
(waitFrame()) the checker keeps a program from redefining, and string and
template literals (`TICK ${ticks:1}`) with their ${...} fields. Constructs
that are still undecided are simply absent — an unmatched keyword costs a
word that does not colour, not a broken file. The language server layers
semantic tokens over this once it reports them. Keep this in step with
packages/compiler: a new keyword, type, literal form, or reserved builtin
there belongs here too (see the repository's AGENTS.md).

patterns.comment: A template string: `TICK ${ticks % 10:1} OPTION ${option}`. Each ${...} field holds an ordinary expression (coloured as source, via the same rules as the file) and an optional :width — see packages/compiler/src/ir's template layout.
patterns.name: string.template.8bs

patterns.comment: The :width after a field's expression — how many cells it takes.
Hexadecimal, in both the C spelling and the 6502-assembly spelling.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.hex.8bs

patterns.comment: Binary, likewise: bit patterns are written constantly on this hardware.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.binary.8bs

patterns.comment: A decimal fraction such as 0.5 — legal only as the first argument to #frames(...), the compiler's compile-time duration function; the language has no other float syntax.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.decimal.fraction.8bs

patterns.comment: Sized integers: the MySQL-inspired canonical spelling (tinyint/smallint/mediumint/int, u-prefixed for unsigned) plus the short systems-programming alias (i8/u8...).
patterns.name: support.type.primitive.8bs

patterns.comment: The name in `function name(` is the definition, not a call.
The name bound by `let x` / `const x`.
The name in `namespace screen {` — the surface a caller writes `screen.setColors(...)` against.

#frames(...), the compile-time duration function (packages/compiler/src/fold) — the `#` is the spelling for anything 8bitscript evaluates before the target sees it — as a region so its unit word can be coloured only where it *is* a unit: `seconds` is not a reserved name, it is the required second argument — #frames(0.5, seconds) — and anywhere else it is an ordinary identifier.
#system(), the compile-time machine (packages/compiler/src/fold): the number of the machine a build is for, to compare with the names @8bitscript/system exports.
Any other #name: the compile-time spelling, coloured as such so a reader sees it is not a runtime call (the compiler reports one it does not know).
patterns.name: support.function.compile-time.8bs

patterns.comment: waitFrame() (packages/compiler/src/ir), the reserved runtime builtin function.
patterns.name: support.function.builtin.8bs

patterns.comment: An identifier immediately followed by `(` reads as a call.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.call.8bs

patterns.comment: The colon introducing a type annotation.
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.type.8bs

patterns.comment: Hardware placement and similar attributes, e.g. @address(0x900F).
patterns.name: entity.name.function.decorator.8bs
